title: Wezterm fails to start, emits Resource temporarily unavailable
body:
### What Operating System(s) are you seeing this problem on?

Linux Wayland

### Which Wayland compositor or X11 Window manager(s) are you using?

Hyprland nightly (built from commit 015664eb4cde5ab93cfacbfd8c2e831eeb876634). Current Nixos unstable version on 2023-10-23.

### WezTerm version

20230712-072601-f4abf8fd

### Did you try the latest nightly build to see if the issue is better (or worse!) than your current version?

Yes, and I updated the version box above to show the version of the nightly that I tried

### Describe the bug

Wezterm fails to start and a notification is sent with this error:

```
ERROR  wezterm_gui > running message loop: error during event_q.dispatch protocol_error=None: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11); terminating
```



### To Reproduce

Try to run: `wezterm --skip-config`

### Configuration

no config

### Expected Behavior

Wezterm window starts like normal.

### Logs

No output is produced when starting from a shell.

### Anything else?

```
Linux 6.5.7 #1-NixOS SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue Oct 10 20:03:06 UTC 2023 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```

Using AMD GPU for graphics. It's working with acceleration and similar.

This happened when bumping my lockfiles for nixos and installed the latest version of everything. Hyprland jumped from around the 0.29 release and into [0.31](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/releases/tag/v0.31.0), essentially.

RE: Wezterm I'm unsure how it moved version-wise, but perhaps I could find out if that would help. I'll jump back to my previous build for now in order to be productive today, so I can update which version I actually used before.

comments.body:
Found a fix for me that doesn't involve `config.enable_wayland = false`.
System: Fedora 39, wezterm 20230712-072601-f4abf8fd, Nvidia GPU.

1 - Uninstall WezTerm in the Software app
2 - Install Nouveau drivers for your gpu (a whole annoying process within itself)
3 - Download Wezterm with dnf [link](https://wezfurlong.org/wezterm/install/linux.html#installing-on-fedora-and-rpm-based-systems-via-copr)

If this doesn't work, `config.enable_wayland = false` but I didn't like the gnome window header at the top, this fixes that. GL

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
> this should be worked upon by the developers. There has not been any update on this issue here by any main developer.

I'm not sure if you are aware of how entitled this sounds.

As I've mentioned elsewhere in the issue tracker, wayland support in wezterm is not in good shape currently and requires significant effort to get into better shape because the wayland ecosystem crates dramatically changed their API.

I do not have time or inclination to do this work, but if sufficient sponsorship materializes to fund it, then I will consider making time for it. I would appreciate a set of PRs that do this work.

Regarding the status of this issue: the issue reported by the OP was resolved for the OP at the time it was evaluated.
If you are having an issue, and it doesn't appear to be covered by an existing open issue, then you are encouraged to open a new one with all relevant information.

comments.author: participant17
comments.body:
> > this should be worked upon by the developers. There has not been any update on this issue here by any main developer.
> 
> I'm not sure if you are aware of how entitled this sounds.
> 
Couldn't agree more.  If someone is willing to work on this, for free, in their own time, then that would be wonderful.  If not - that's entirely reasonable, I don't recollect paying for any support or anyone promising to provide it for free.

> I do not have time or inclination to do this work, but if sufficient sponsorship materializes to fund it, then I will consider making time for it. I would appreciate a set of PRs that do this work.
The same applies for me unfortunately.  One thing though which _did_ jump out at me in the Hyprland diff of `window.cpp` is this:
```
            g_pCompositor->setPreferredScaleForSurface(surf, PMONITOR ? PMONITOR->scale : 1.f);
            g_pCompositor->setPreferredTransformForSurface(surf, PMONITOR->transform);
```
Note that the first line [which is just the removal of the `m_pFractionalScaleProtocolManager` property from the previous code] ensures that `PMONITOR` isn't null before dereferencing the `scale` member.  However, the second line [which is new] does NOT perform this check.  I immediately wonder if there's a possibility of `PMONITOR` being null inside Hyprland, resulting in Bad Things happening when this code runs.  No more than a wild guess based on a 30-second look at the diff though!!!
